what_the_delta_does: Owned workspace: freeze_generation_context(owned_workspace=...) requires an absent or empty root, records {cell_id, cell_contract_sha256, root, root_identity [st_dev, st_ino]} in generation-workspace.json; every later control step re-asserts the directory identity and the declared absolute root (WORKSPACE_ROOT_IDENTITY_CHANGED), so a cloned or replaced root cannot reuse the marker.

Terminal marker: the RETIRING marker file is the quota module's GENERATION_TERMINAL_NAME, so reopen_generation_context and publication_lease refuse a retired or retiring generation (GENERATION_WORKSPACE_TERMINAL, SPOOL_GENERATION_TERMINAL) under the same quota lock; the reservation guard is now created inside that lock after the terminal check, which also removes the old guard-before-lock orphan.

Retirement holds the original quota lock for its whole duration, refuses live reservations and any reservation guard, and try-locks every declared units.lock with the original kernel lock, refusing an active writer and keeping the lock inode.

Fence: an external caller-written file whose sha the caller passes; it must bind this workspace owner sha, carry released and eligible flags with every authority False, bind generation context, run id and cell, and name end-grid rows that the module reads back through pm_end_grid.read_end_grid, matching row sha, cell id and job binding sha, with the retained view contract loaded when present; the grid root must not overlap the working root in either direction.

Inventory: regular files only, hard links refused, reparse refused, bounded by paths, nodes and bytes; a file or directory is owned only if it matches the spool's own layout (objects/sha256/xx/<sha>.<ext> with prefix consistency, symbols/<sha>/domains/<sha>/manifest.json, tmp/<hex>.part) or is a declared direct file; parts named real_control, STOP or .git are never owned; anything else refuses before any unlink.

Intent then unlink: the intent lists every file with identity and bytes, the marker binds the intent sha and the arguments, a second inventory must match the intent record for record, each file is identity-checked immediately before unlink, a third inventory must be empty, directories are removed deepest first with identity checks while parents of retained unit locks stay, then the external receipt (ARCHIVED_RECORD_ONLY, payloads_retained False, genuine_cold_reopen_available False, four authorities False) and the completion marker are published and the intent is deleted. Resume with changed arguments is refused; a changed leaf after intent is refused and preserved.
checks: Deletion can only reach files under a root that carries the owner marker created on an empty directory, that match the owned layout or the caller's explicit list, and that are listed in the intent with unchanged identity; the published data tree, the retained graphs, the trim QA folder, the WFV protocol and the STOP capsule can never sit inside such a root, and protected paths are additionally refused if they overlap the root in either direction.
The end-grid readback ties DELETE to a recorded RESULT: no row, wrong sha, wrong cell or wrong job binding refuses with RETIREMENT_GRID_READBACK_REQUIRED.

Interruption: before the marker, a rerun recomputes the same intent and the write-once publish compares bytes (RETIREMENT_CONTROL_CONFLICT if different); after the marker, resume is bound to the intent sha and arguments; after the external receipt but before completion, the receipt republish compares equal because the body is deterministic.
Lock order inside _retirement_unit_locks releases the kernel lock before closing the handle (ExitStack LIFO).

The test file exercises every refusal named above with invented owned I/O under FXPM_DERIVED_QA_ROOT, asserts that payloads are never re-hashed during retirement, and checks the admission race against the same real lock.

findings.text: The owned layout covers only what pm_authority_spool itself writes. The orchestration and producer write declared-slots/<sha>/precommit.json, requests/<cell>/<slot>/<attempt>.json, <cell>/commits/NN.json, terminal.json, run-receipt.json, attempts/<slot>/<attempt>.json, m5-source-context.json and declared-cell-source/<sha>/<cell> under the same root (producer 2716 to 3567, orchestration 3186 to 4064). None matches _retirement_owned, so a real declared workspace retires only if the worker enumerates every such file in owned_direct_files; otherwise RETIREMENT_FOREIGN_DIRECTORY or RETIREMENT_FOREIGN_FILE refuses before any unlink. Correct and fail-closed for this component; the worker's enumeration must be checked against the real write set, including the attempts tree, which can hold hundreds of files per slot, against max_paths.

retired_payload_files and retired_logical_bytes in the receipt are taken from the intent, not from what this process unlinked. After an interruption followed by an external removal the receipt overstates. Count the actual unlinks or name the fields as intent counts.

A stale .generation-quota.* temp file or any other unowned leftover blocks retirement with RETIREMENT_FOREIGN_FILE until removed by hand. That is the no-reaping rule the handoff states; the code should be documented as the operator-visible outcome.

read_generation_retirement re-verifies the fence, re-reads the symbol's grid file and reloads the view contract on every read after completion. Small today; it is the one read on this path that grows with the grid.
